text:
ryan-cs: FYI AcmeHealth reported a big perf regression after we flipped them to the new int4 quantized model this morning. p95 doubled and some responses look garbled compared to their fp16 baseline. They observed it on /v1/generate: request IDs 8f3a2b, 8f3a2f.

emma-eng: Can you paste one of the failing request payloads + a minimal input we can repro with? Also which deployment (dedicated vs hosted) and region?

ryan-cs: Paste below. Dedicated pool acme-prod-eu-west. Sample input: 
```\n{"prompt": "Summarize clinical trial findings about drug X in two bullets"}\n```
Output from int4: 
```\n"findings: drug x trial positive \u0000 data corrupted"\n```
FP16 output is correct and fast. Affected since ~09:10 UTC.

luis-ml: I pulled perf traces for the two request IDs. Quick summary: int4 path is repeatedly switching kernels mid-inference and we see lots of small memcpy ops. NVTX shows tiny kernels + CPU fallback in KV-cache hotpath. Snippet from profiler: 
```\n[trace] kernel_select: select kernel=int4_conv_fast (seq_len=32, batch=1)\n[trace] runtime: fallback to kernel=int4_emulate_fp16 (reason=kv_align_mismatch)\n[trace] memcpy_h2d 1.2ms\n[trace] launch kernel=int4_emulate_fp16 5.4ms\n[trace] memcpy_d2h 0.8ms\n```\nLooks like KV-cache alignment check is forcing a compatibility slow path that emulates fp16.

daniel-runtime: That matches a thing we saw in canary last week — when kv cache chunking doesn't match the compiled kernel layout we trigger a safe (slower) execution path. For dedicated pools we sometimes see different torchscript layout due to HW packing. Two immediate checks: 1) artifact compilation flags (tensor_align, pack_stride), 2) whether customer traffic hits a mixture of model variants (eg model:v12-int4 vs model:v12-int4-alt).

emma-eng: How bad is the memcpy overhead? If memcopy is the main culprit we can mitigate by routing them to a node with matching compile artifacts or temporarily pin to fp16.

luis-ml: Memcopy dominates on p95 for those traces; end-to-end int4 is ~3-4x slower than expected because we bounce between kernels. Also calibration step for this customer's workload produced a wide scale distribution so some layers used fp8-ish fallbacks which further forces slow kernels.

tia-platform: We can do two quick mitigations: (A) pin customer routing policy to fp16 model variant for the dedicated pool (zero downtime) or (B) set a node-level flag to disable the kv_align check which makes int4 path optimistic (risky). I recommend (A) as safe short-term. I can push routing change in ~10m if eng approves.

daniel-runtime: +1 for pinning to fp16. For a longer-term fix I'll open a runtime patch to relax the strict alignment check and add a fast-path validator that runs once per model load instead of per-request. That should remove per-request fallback. Patch will need perf tests.

emma-eng: I'll apply the fp16 pin for AcmeHealth now and confirm their p95. Ryan, can you tell them we're trying a safe rollback to fp16 while we investigate?

ryan-cs: Yep, I'll message them: "We're routing your traffic back to the fp16 variant immediately to restore latency and correctness. We're investigating an int4 artifact mismatch that caused a slow fallback; we'll follow up with a root cause and ETA for a safe int4 rollback." :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Deployment note: route update for acme-prod-eu-west -> model:v12-fp16 scheduled, initiated by emma-eng, change id c3d9fa.

luis-ml: After the pin we should re-run calibration with a constrained per-layer clipping (narrower quant ranges) and a fixed seed to avoid dynamic fallback. Also I'll run a synthetic microbench: batch sweep [1,2,4,8] and seq sweep [16,32,64] to reproduce kernel switches.

daniel-runtime: Action items: (1) emma apply routing pin (done) (2) luis run calibration + microbench and share profile (ETA 6h) (3) daniel open runtime PR to change alignment check + add unit/perf tests (ETA 24-48h) (4) tia confirm customer routing applied and collect p95 numbers (ETA 30m).

emma-eng: Routing applied. Initial p95 for their production node dropped back to baseline within two reports (customer confirmed). I captured a post-change trace — no memcpy storm, kernel_select stayed on fp16.

ryan-cs: Customer replied: "latency restored, outputs look normal, thanks." I'll close the urgent ticket and ask if they'd like int4 re-evaluation later.

luis-ml: I'll post the microbench results and the calibration recipe to the eng-runtime channel when ready. Preliminary hypothesis: miscompiled int4 kernel + broad calibration ranges -> runtime fallback loop.

daniel-runtime: Noted. We'll prioritize a conservative fast-path for kv cache compatibility checks to avoid per-request decisions. Adding perf tests to catch regressions in canaries.

ryan-cs: Thanks everyone. I'll send a customer-facing summary after we have the next steps and ETA for int4 re-enable. :white_check_mark:
